owner.occupation: Trademark and patent attorney (benrishi), Chinese-speaking clients practice

world.bio: I am a benrishi (Japanese patent and trademark attorney) based in Kanda, Tokyo. I spent two years in Beijing at Peking University's law school in my twenties, and my Mandarin is good enough for contract negotiation. Over the last three years I have built a quiet practice around small Chinese manufacturers entering Japan: trademark searches, filings, oppositions, and dealing with the Japan Patent Office on their behalf. I work mostly in Mandarin, with documents in Japanese.
skills_assets: Registered benrishi with eleven years of experience; formerly at a mid-sized IP firm, independent for three years
Handles Japanese trademark filings and oppositions for small Chinese manufacturers, works in Mandarin
A small office in Kanda with one paralegal and one part-time translator (Japanese-Chinese)
Working relationships with two Chinese law firms in Shenzhen and Hangzhou for cross-border referrals
A set of bilingual templates: trademark search report, JPO office-action response, opposition notice

projects.name: Opposition for a Zhejiang kettle maker
projects.text: A kettle manufacturer from Yongkang filed a trademark in Japan two years ago, and a Tokyo distributor has filed a nearly identical mark in the same class. I am drafting an opposition with evidence of prior use in China, which is not easy because the JPO prefers use in Japan. The opposition deadline is 14 November. Estimated fee about 480,000 yen.

projects.name: Bilingual guide for Chinese SMEs
projects.text: I want to write a short guide, maybe twenty pages, in simplified Chinese, called something like 'Five mistakes Chinese factories make when registering a mark in Japan'. A friend at a Shenzhen law firm said she would proofread. I have an outline and three case studies, but no time to write the second half.

notes.text: Long day at the office. A client from Guangdong called at 8pm Tokyo time, asking if his mark would be rejected because it sounds like a Japanese word. It does sound like one. I explained phonetic similarity for twenty minutes and he said 'so what do I do?' I said choose another name. He said the name was his late father's. That one will take time.
Trained for the lottery run by the Tokyo Marathon. Ran 12 km along the Sumida. Didn't hit the pace I wanted. I may not even win the lottery, but I like the routine.
Called my mother in Shizuoka. Dad forgot what day it was again, asked me three times if I had eaten. She laughed on the phone, but I could hear her voice shake. I told her I'll come down in October.

Bought a Pilot Custom 823 at a small shop in Ochanomizu. Amber barrel, medium nib. Spent more than I planned. My wife said that is the fourth one this year. I said it is the third, because one was a gift.

Reviewed a Japanese-Chinese translation of an office action. The translator rendered 'distinctiveness' as a term that is used in patent law but not trademark law. Corrected it. These small errors can cost a client a month.

A new inquiry from a toy manufacturer in Shantou. They want to file in classes 28 and 35. I told them the fee, they asked for a discount. I held the price. In my experience people who bargain at the start also bargain at every invoice.

Dinner with an old classmate from Beijing, now working in a Tokyo trading company. He said business with China is quiet this year. I said mine is the opposite, small makers are expanding quietly into Japan because the American market looks risky.

Spent the morning on the opposition draft. Kettle brand's evidence is mostly invoices and catalogue pages in Chinese. I need certified translations, which adds cost. Called my translator to ask for a quote.

messages.text:
Wang: Kenji, do you have time for a call on the 15th?
Me: Yes, afternoon Japan time works.
Wang: I have a client making LED strips, wants to register in Japan.
Me: Send me the details and I'll run a search first.

Mother: Your father asked about you today.
Me: What did he say?
Mother: He said, 'Is Kenji still in China?' I said no, he's in Tokyo.
Me: I'll come on the 10th.

Sato: The JPO sent notice for the kettle opposition, they accepted the filing.
Me: Good, thank you. Please file the power of attorney.
Sato: Already in the folder.

Client: Kenji-san, when will the opposition be ready?
Me: Draft next week, final by 7 November.
Client: Can we speed up?
Me: I will try, but the evidence translation takes time.

relations.about: Seventy-four, early dementia, mother takes care of him
Lawyer in Shenzhen who refers clients to him
Paralegal in his office, Japanese, studied Chinese

constraints: Does not take cases outside trademarks and patents
Fixed hourly rate; does not discount for new clients
Cannot travel to China before December
sensitive: His father's dementia is getting worse and he feels guilty for living far away
Some clients delay paying invoices for months
He worries that the market for small Chinese clients will dry up if the economy turns
